observation_summary: The application crashes with an OutOfMemoryError when processing a large number of data points (40,000) because the Weight class creates a full N x N matrix (1.6 billion elements) to store diagonal weights.
hypothesis: The Weight class incorrectly represents a diagonal weight matrix as a full N x N dense matrix, leading to O(N^2) memory consumption. For large datasets, this causes an OutOfMemoryError. The fix requires using a specialized DiagonalMatrix representation to reduce memory usage to O(N).
prediction: The Weight constructor will be shown to instantiate a full BlockRealMatrix of size N x N, where N is the number of observations, instead of a more memory-efficient structure.
experiment_rationale: The bug report and stack trace clearly indicate that the memory exhaustion occurs during the instantiation of a large matrix within the Weight class constructor. The fix involves changing the underlying data structure from a dense matrix to a diagonal one, which is an algorithmic improvement in memory efficiency.
reasoning_summary: The failure is a classic memory exhaustion issue caused by an inefficient algorithmic choice (using a dense matrix for diagonal data). The fix replaces this with a sparse/diagonal representation, which is a change in the computational strategy (Algorithm/Method).

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While a new class (DiagonalMatrix) was introduced, the root cause is the inefficient algorithmic choice of using a dense matrix for diagonal data, which is a procedural/computational strategy issue.
